articles.title: Babystar review – a new arrival upends camera-ready life in disturbing family influencer satire
articles.summary: Every ethical issue surrounding parents vlogging their kids’ childhoods for money is raised in Joscha Bongard’s debut, but it releases the dysfunctional tension too easily. When teenager Luca (Maja Bons) wants to watch the film of her birth, she finds it on YouTube.
body: Sixteen-year-old Luca is the only child of Stella (Bea Brocks) and Chris (Liliom Lewald), social media stars who make viral videos of their perfect-looking family life for their 4 million followers. They live in a beautiful, sterile minimalist home in the countryside, and we often watch them through CCTV cameras fitted in every room. Shrewdly, first time film-maker Joscha Bongard doesn’t portray Stella and Chris as monsters; they love their daughter Luca, who they affectionately call Nunki. But fundamentally they do their best parenting in front of the camera, all bright smiles and proud affectionate glances.
points: Every ethical issue surrounding parents vlogging their kids’ childhoods for money is raised in Joscha Bongard’s debut, but it releases the dysfunctional tension too easily.
When teenager Luca (Maja Bons) wants to watch the film of her birth, she finds it on YouTube.

articles.title: Apple Reveals Apple Music Hall, a New Live Venue in London
articles.summary: Apple is bringing a new live music venue to London. Located in Battersea Power Station, Apple Music Hall is a state-of-the-art venue “designed to connect artists and fans through bespoke, intimate performances unlike anywhere else,” Apple said in its announcement on Tuesday.
body: Apple Music Hall is also an operational production facility, with two recording and mixing studios built to professional standards. The venue is hardwired for 16+ cameras with a broadcast control room that also supports iPhone video capture.

“In short, an artist can perform an intimate live show for fans at Apple Music Hall and walk out with a finished Spatial Audio recording, a broadcast-ready mix, and multicamera video — all from a single show,” a press release states. “Performances out of Apple Music Hall will also be livestreamed globally so fans outside of London can tune in to enjoy these one-time-only shows from their favorite artists.”

“At Apple Music, we care deeply about music, the artists who make it and their life stories,” added Zane Lowe, Apple Music’s global creative director and lead anchor for Apple Music 1. “We’re always looking for new opportunities to connect the artists and the fans because we are fans. What better way to celebrate this relationship than a new music venue where we get to experience amazing music in an amazing space and share it with the world. Great music and memories will be made at Apple Music Hall.”

articles.title: Susan Sarandon to Be Honored at Rome Film Festival Sidebar Where ‘The Accompanist’ Will Bow Internationally (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Susan Sarandon will be honored by the Rome Film Festival’s independently run Alice in the City sidebar, which is dedicated to films for children and youth. Sarandon will be attending the Eternal City fest to promote the international launch of “Silicon Valley” star Zach Woods’ feature film debut…
body: Susan Sarandon will be honored by the Rome Film Festival ’s independently run Alice in the City sidebar, which is dedicated to films for children and youth.

“From ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’ to ‘The Hunger,’ from ‘The Witches of Eastwick’ to ‘Thelma & Louise,’ to ‘Dead Man Walking,’ Sarandon has spanned decades of cinema, building a gallery of female characters that cannot be reduced to a single model,” the fest said in a statement praising her career. The statement added that the characters she plays in these films are all “Women who question identity, desire, power, rules and freedom.” “But the common thread running through her journey is not only the roles she has chosen,” it continued.

“It is also her ability to maintain her own autonomy from the Hollywood system, bringing together artistic choices, personal freedom and consistency of her own convictions,” the statement went on to point out.

Sarandon, who recently attended the Venice Film Festival in September with her latest film, Italian director Andrea Pallaoro’s “The Echo Chamber,” said in Venice that she continues to be shunned by Hollywood over her outspoken support of Palestine.

articles.title: Parvathy Thiruvothu on Playing a Police Officer in ‘Pradhama Drishtiya Kuttakkar’ and Speaking Out About Misogyny Despite Scrutiny: ‘I Enjoy Watching Patriarchy Fall Apart’
articles.summary: Indian actor Parvathy Thiruvothu has spent two decades fighting the system from outside it – both on screen and off. In “Pradhama Drishtiya Kuttakkar” (“Prima Facie Guilty”), the Shahad Nilambur-directed thriller now running in theaters, she’s finally on the inside, portraying a police officer for…
body: Thiruvothu, whose credits include “Bangalore Days,” “Take Off,” “Uyare” and “Virus,” has built a two-decade career largely on roles that push against the structures around her characters.

In “Pradhama Drishtiya Kuttakkar,” produced by Arjun Selva under 11 Icons Film Productions, Thiruvothu plays Aleena Abraham, a woman who becomes a police officer through a compassionate appointment after the death of her husband, also a constable. Set largely inside a local police station, the film follows Aleena alongside fellow officers Divya, Dasan and Sreenath as an unexpected criminal case upends the precinct, testing perceptions of guilt, duty and systemic justice. The film’s plot repeatedly asks how quickly an audience decides someone’s guilt based on incomplete evidence.

Thiruvothu says the film departs from convention by revealing the central crime within its first 10 to 15 minutes, shifting the tension from whodunit to whether the officers involved will be found out.

Thiruvothu has not watched “Santosh,” Sandhya Suri’s Cannes-debuting film in which Shahana Goswami plays a policewoman who takes up her late husband’s post through a similar compassionate appointment.

articles.title: How fields of Fermanagh helped Daisy Edgar-Jones prepare for her latest film
articles.summary: The actor, whose mum is from County Down, recalls long childhood summers in Northern Ireland.
body: Actor Daisy Edgar-Jones is no stranger to Ireland, having spent five months in the country filming hit drama Normal People which was released in 2020.

But it was actually fields in County Fermanagh, where some of her family live, that helped her prepare for the role of beloved character Elinor Dashwood in Jane Austen's Sense and Sensibility, some 20 years before.
Her mother is from County Down and Edgar-Jones spent her childhood roaming fields in Northern Ireland.

"I remember big long summers when I was very young in Fermanagh in the fields which definitely helped with my Sense and Sensibility journey because I was doing a lot of the similar wandering around, with not much to do, under the big sky and I love being here," she told BBC News NI.

articles.title: Apple Music to open concert venue in Battersea
articles.summary: The tech giant has built its own concert hall, but says its not in competition with small venues.
body: The US tech giant Apple is to open a new, state-of-the-art concert hall in London, situated underneath its UK headquarters at Battersea Power Station.
The 600-capacity venue will host one-off shows by major recording artists and new bands, all of which will be filmed and broadcast live online.

Apple Music's vice president, Oliver Schusser, told BBC News the facility, which is expected to open in the coming weeks, contained "more cameras and speakers than any venue of its size, anywhere in the world".
It comes as London's live music scene faces huge pressure, with 45 venues closing in the capital last year alone.

articles.title: David Tennant Starred In One Of The Worst HBO Miniseries Ever
articles.summary: HBO has a long tradition of quality miniseries and high-profile, short-lived TV productions. This show starring David Tennant isn't one of them.
body: The 2018 HBO miniseries "Camping" was created by Lena Dunham and Jenni Konner, and was based on the 2016 British series of the same name. The series ostensibly focuses on a character named Walt, played by David Tennant, who is celebrating his 45th birthday by going on a camping trip in the California woods. His wife, Kathryn (Jennifer Garner), however, is the real protagonist, as she is a famed influencer and is immensely shrill and controlling. Joining them on the trip are Kathryn's sister (Ione Skye), a mutual friend named Miguel (Arturo Del Puerto), Miguel's woo-woo girlfriend (Juliette Lewis), and a few others (Janicza Bravo, Brett Gelman, Chris Sullivan).
points: HBO has a long tradition of quality miniseries and high-profile, short-lived TV productions.
This show starring David Tennant isn't one of them.

articles.title: Sense and Sensibility review – Daisy Edgar-Jones leads sober-minded next-gen do-over of Austen romcom
articles.summary: With Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles as the Dashwood sisters, this fresh take on a beloved classic is not to be confused with Ang Lee’s. There’s no reason for anyone working on a new adaptation of Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility to be intimidated by the celebrated 1995 movie by director Ang…
body: The sisters at the heart of the story, Elinor and Marianne Dashwood, played in 1995 by Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet, are now played by Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles, and frankly don’t look and sound much like the sisters we thought we knew. They look like young women who knew each other reasonably well at uni and are now in a flatshare in London. It is a story of financial and romantic crisis. Mrs Dashwood and her three daughters, having happily occupied a handsome Sussex estate, are forced to move to humble Barton Cottage in Devon when Mrs Dashwood’s stepson John Dashwood inherits their property and effectively evicted them.

Before this can happen, Elinor meets and falls for young Edward Ferrars, a shy and decent young man of a well-to-do family, reticently portrayed by George MacKay. Here, in fact, it should be said that Diana Reid’s script and Georgia Oakley’s direction put into valuably sharper focus something left unstressed in 1995: that Mrs Dashwood (Caitríona Balfe) is pointedly insisting on moving away to the west country rather than endure the indignity of her daughter seeming to be a gold-digger.

articles.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico file lawsuit against Trump's White House ban
articles.summary: Major US networks later suspended White House TV coverage of Trump as he headed to New York for a UN summit.
body: CNN, Politico and MS NOW have said they will sue the Trump administration after the US media outlets were barred from the White House.

President Donald Trump announced the ban on Friday, accusing the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his team. The companies said their reporters were denied access to the building on Saturday.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".
The White House later launched a streaming channel, Trump TV, after major US networks suspended their pooled coverage of the president ahead of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
